subject: Velosys mid-cycle uplift — options for priority billing, co-terming, and voucher approach
messages:
From: Samira Patel <samira@velosys.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 1 Sep 2026 10:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-cycle capacity top-up & co-term options

Hi Karthik —

Quick one from our side. Usage spiked in August (attached) and we need to add committed capacity mid-cycle. We'd like to understand: 1) how you price a straight top-up (pro-rated) vs. 2) an uplift with voucher/credit offset vs. 3) annualize and co-term the account now.

Key constraints: procurement wants minimal invoice churn, engineering needs predictable SLAs for the next quarter, and we need to keep unit cost near current blended rates if possible.

Can you send a short matrix of options + recommended path? If easier, we can do a quick call — Eric (cc'd) handles procurement.

Thanks,
Samira
Samira Patel
Head of Platform Engineering
Velosys Inc.
[Attachment: Velosys-usage-report-Aug.xlsx]

Subject: Re: Mid-cycle capacity top-up & co-term options

Samira — thanks for the note and the usage file. We're happy to lay out the three paths and recommend one based on your priorities. Ben and Kim will put together the pricing matrix; can we tentatively set a call for Thursday 9/3 at 10am PT to walk through?

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 2 Sep 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Mid-cycle capacity top-up & co-term options

Attaching a compact options packet (see attachment) — high level:

- Option A: Pro-rated top-up (fastest) — charge remaining months pro-rated, no change to term. No discount; unit price = current list.
- Option B: Staged uplift + voucher (recommended if Velosys wants blended economics) — add committed capacity now with a voucher credit that offsets part of the uplift for the first 3 months; gives lower blended unit cost for Q4, keeps invoice simple (one amendment + monthly true-up).
- Option C: Annualize & co-term — convert to an annualized commit at an 8% uplift (volume discount baked in) and co-term to a single renewal date. Best long-term unit cost but requires procurement sign-off for updated annual commitment.

Pros/cons and estimated financials are in Velosys-topup-options.pdf. I noted the SLA priority and included a recommended SLO add-on for burst capacity.

- Ben
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
[Attachment: Velosys-topup-options.pdf]

From: Samira Patel <samira@velosys.ai>

Cc: Eric Huang <eric@velosys.ai>
Date: Thu, 3 Sep 2026 11:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Mid-cycle capacity top-up & co-term options

Thanks Ben — looks good. A couple of clarifying questions from procurement:

• For Option B (voucher), how is the voucher applied on the invoice? Is it a one-time credit line item or monthly amortized credit?
• If we do Option C (annualize), can you show a simple comparison (12-month spend) against Option B with the voucher applied? We want to ensure we don't end up paying materially more in total cash this year.

Also, our legal will need standard amendment language for a mid-cycle commit — do you have a short form we can start with?

Happy to take the 9/3 slot if you want to run through live — Eric and I will be on.

Samira

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Samira Patel <samira@velosys.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 4 Sep 2026 08:50:00 -07:00
Subject: Quote + comparison (Option A / B / C)

Hi Samira — attaching the quote workbook and a side-by-side comparison (Quote-Velosys-Q3-2026.xlsx). Quick answers:

• Voucher mechanics: we issue a one-time invoice credit that can be applied across the next three monthly invoices (amortized on the invoice as a negative line item). If you prefer a single credit up front, we can do that too.
• Comparison: Option B (staged uplift + voucher) yields a ~6.7% blended reduction vs. Option A this quarter; Option C (annualize) yields ~9.5% blended on a 12-month view but requires committing budget now and a single co-term amendment.

Link to DocuSign for the amendment/quote: https://www.docusign.net/Member/PowerFormSigning.aspx?PowerFormId=abc123-velosys-quote

If Velosys prefers minimal invoice churn and wants the engineering SLA immediately, our recommendation is Option B (staged uplift + voucher) — it preserves flexibility and reduces short-term unit cost without a full annual commitment. I included language for a short-form amendment in the workbook.

Attachments: Quote-Velosys-Q3-2026.xlsx

Happy to hop on the call Thursday to walk the file.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Sr. Pricing & Revenue Ops

From: Samira Patel <samira@velosys.ai>

2) Send the short-form amendment and a PO-ready invoice so our procurement team can issue payment and tie to the PO.

We'll sign the DocuSign once we have the amendment and PO format. Looking forward to getting the SLA in place for the next quarter.
